summary.business_problem: The current system lacks a reliable, compliant payment processing workflow that ensures timely handling of payment webhooks, maintains financial audit integrity, and provides clear failure and refund handling for customers.
summary.proposed_solution: Implement a payment processing workflow that integrates with Stripe to handle order creation, payment initiation, webhook receipt, failure handling, and refund processing. The system will ensure audit logging, compliance with financial retention standards, and secure handling of payment data without storing raw card information.

in_scope: Customer can create an order and initiate payment for the order total.
System integrates with Stripe as the payment provider for card payments.
System creates a payment record in a 'pending' state before redirecting the customer to the payment provider.
System exposes a webhook endpoint to receive asynchronous payment status callbacks from Stripe.
Incoming webhook callbacks are verified using Stripe's signature scheme before processing.
System handles out-of-order or duplicate webhook deliveries without double-crediting an order.
On payment failure, the order is marked as 'payment failed' and the customer can retry payment with the same order.
The system records the provider's failure reason code for every failed payment attempt.
A Support Agent can issue a full or partial refund for a completed payment.
Refund amounts do not exceed the original captured payment amount.
The customer receives an email notification when a refund is issued.
Every payment state transition is recorded in an immutable audit log with timestamp and actor.
Payment webhook processing completes within 2 seconds under normal load conditions.
Payment audit logs are retained for a minimum of 7 years for financial compliance.
The system is resilient to temporary Stripe API unavailability during order creation.
Payment processing depends on the order-creation flow being completed first.
Refund functionality is only available when a payment has been in a 'captured' state.
out_of_scope: Support for any payment provider other than Stripe.
Implementation of a payment processing system that handles card data storage.
Development of a customer-facing interface for managing refunds or viewing payment history beyond the email notification.
Integration with any third-party financial reporting or accounting systems.
future_scope: Evaluation of alternative payment providers for future releases.
Implementation of real-time payment status visibility for customers.
Expansion of refund policies to include partial refunds for non-completed orders.
assumptions: The system will be accessible via a public internet-facing endpoint to receive webhooks and serve customer-facing pages.
The shared secret for webhook signature verification will be configured with Stripe at deployment time.
constraints: Only Stripe is in scope for this release.
A prolonged Stripe outage could block all new order payments platform-wide.
Without proper idempotency, duplicate webhook deliveries could result in double-fulfillment of orders.
The definition of 'normal load' for webhook processing is not specified in the requirements.
The format of the failure reason code to be recorded is not specified.
The content and delivery mechanism for refund email notifications are not specified.
The definition of 'immutable audit log' and its implementation method are not specified.
The retention duration of payment audit logs is specified as a minimum of 7 years, not a maximum.

epics.title: Payment Order Creation and Initiation
epics.objective: Enable customers to create an order and initiate payment for the order total.
epics.business_value: Allows customers to proceed with purchasing items through the platform.

epics.title: Stripe Integration and Payment Flow Management
epics.objective: Establish a secure and reliable integration with Stripe to process card payments and manage payment records.
epics.business_value: Provides a compliant and secure payment processing mechanism using Stripe.

epics.title: Webhook Endpoint and Callback Processing
epics.objective: Expose a webhook endpoint to receive asynchronous payment status callbacks from Stripe and verify them using Stripe's signature scheme.
epics.business_value: Ensures reliable and secure receipt of payment status updates from Stripe.

epics.title: Handling Out-of-Order and Duplicate Webhook Deliveries
epics.objective: Implement logic to prevent double-crediting of orders by handling out-of-order or duplicate webhook deliveries correctly.
epics.business_value: Avoids financial inaccuracies and order fulfillment errors due to duplicate or out-of-sequence callbacks.

epics.title: Payment Failure Handling and Retry Capability
epics.objective: Mark orders as 'payment failed' upon failure and allow customers to retry payment with the same order.
epics.business_value: Improves customer experience by enabling retry functionality after payment failure.

epics.title: Refund Processing by Support Agents
epics.objective: Enable Support Agents to issue full or partial refunds for completed payments, with amounts not exceeding the original captured amount.
epics.business_value: Provides a mechanism for customer service to resolve payment issues and support refund requests.

epics.title: Refund Notification to Customer
epics.objective: Send an email notification to the customer when a refund is issued.
epics.business_value: Ensures customers are informed of refund actions, improving transparency and trust.

epics.title: Immutable Audit Logging of Payment State Transitions
epics.objective: Record every payment state transition in an immutable audit log with timestamp and actor.
epics.business_value: Provides a tamper-proof record of payment events for compliance and traceability.

epics.title: Payment Audit Log Retention for Financial Compliance
epics.objective: Ensure payment audit logs are retained for a minimum of 7 years to meet financial compliance standards.
epics.business_value: Meets regulatory requirements for financial data retention and auditability.

epics.title: System Resilience to Temporary Stripe API Unavailability
epics.objective: Ensure the system does not lose orders during temporary Stripe API outages by maintaining order state and processing order creation.
epics.business_value: Improves system reliability and prevents data loss during transient service disruptions.

epics.title: Definition of 'Normal Load' for Webhook Processing
epics.objective: Define what constitutes 'normal load' for webhook processing to ensure the 2-second response time is met under realistic conditions.
epics.business_value: Provides clarity on performance expectations and helps in capacity planning and testing.

epics.title: Failure Reason Code Format for Failed Payments
epics.objective: Specify the format and structure of the failure reason code to be recorded for failed payment attempts.
epics.business_value: Ensures consistency and interoperability with Stripe error codes and facilitates debugging and analytics.

epics.title: Email Notification Content and Delivery for Refunds
epics.objective: Define the content and delivery mechanism for refund email notifications to customers.
epics.business_value: Improves customer communication and ensures clarity and consistency in refund notifications.

epics.title: Definition and Implementation of Immutable Audit Log
epics.objective: Clarify what 'immutable' means and define how the audit log is implemented (e.g., database, blockchain) to ensure data integrity.
epics.business_value: Ensures long-term data integrity and compliance with audit requirements.

epics.title: Behavior of Webhook After Order Fulfillment
epics.objective: Define the expected behavior when a webhook is received after the order has been fulfilled.
epics.business_value: Prevents invalid or misleading state updates and ensures system consistency post-fulfillment.

epics.title: Refund Behavior for Payments in 'Pending' State
epics.objective: Define the behavior when a customer attempts to refund a payment that is still in a 'pending' state.
epics.business_value: Prevents invalid refund operations and ensures refund eligibility is correctly enforced.

epics.title: Public Internet Accessibility for System Endpoints
epics.objective: Assume the system will be accessible via a public internet-facing endpoint to receive webhooks and serve customer-facing pages.
epics.business_value: Enables external communication with Stripe and customer-facing services.

stories.title: As a customer, I want to create an order and initiate payment for the order total, so that I can complete my purchase seamlessly.
stories.story_statement: As a customer, I want to create an order and initiate payment for the order total, so that I can complete my purchase seamlessly.
stories.business_value: Enables customers to proceed with purchases without interruption.

acceptance_criteria.given: A customer navigates to the checkout page and selects items to purchase.
acceptance_criteria.when: The customer submits the order form and completes the checkout process.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system creates an order and initiates payment for the total amount of the order.

stories.title: As a system, I want to integrate with Stripe as the payment provider for card payments, so that card payments can be processed securely and reliably.
stories.story_statement: As a system, I want to integrate with Stripe as the payment provider for card payments, so that card payments can be processed securely and reliably.
stories.business_value: Establishes a secure and reliable payment processing pathway using Stripe.

acceptance_criteria.given: The system is configured to connect to Stripe during deployment.
acceptance_criteria.when: A customer attempts to pay via card at checkout.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system redirects the customer to Stripe's payment page and processes the payment through Stripe.

stories.title: As a system, I want to expose a webhook endpoint to receive asynchronous payment status callbacks from Stripe, so that the system can update order status in real time.
stories.story_statement: As a system, I want to expose a webhook endpoint to receive asynchronous payment status callbacks from Stripe, so that the system can update order status in real time.

acceptance_criteria.when: The system receives the callback via the exposed endpoint.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system processes the callback and updates the order status accordingly.

stories.title: As a system, I want to handle out-of-order or duplicate webhook deliveries without double-crediting an order, so that order state integrity is preserved.
stories.story_statement: As a system, I want to handle out-of-order or duplicate webhook deliveries without double-crediting an order, so that order state integrity is preserved.

acceptance_criteria.given: A webhook callback is delivered out-of-order or in duplicate to the system.
acceptance_criteria.when: The system receives the callback and processes it.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system validates the delivery and does not update the order state if it would result in double-crediting.

stories.title: As a customer, I want to retry payment after a failed payment attempt, so that I can complete my purchase without losing progress.
stories.story_statement: As a customer, I want to retry payment after a failed payment attempt, so that I can complete my purchase without losing progress.

stories.title: As a Support Agent, I want to issue a full or partial refund for a completed payment, so that customers can receive refunds for valid reasons.

acceptance_criteria.when: The agent initiates a full or partial refund request.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system processes the refund request and ensures the amount does not exceed the original captured amount.

stories.title: As a system, I want to send an email notification to the customer when a refund is issued, so that the customer is informed of the refund status.
stories.story_statement: As a system, I want to send an email notification to the customer when a refund is issued, so that the customer is informed of the refund status.
stories.business_value: Provides transparency and timely communication to customers about refund actions.

acceptance_criteria.given: A refund is successfully issued by a support agent.

stories.title: As a system, I want to record every payment state transition in an immutable audit log with timestamp and actor, so that all payment activity is traceable and verifiable.
stories.story_statement: As a system, I want to record every payment state transition in an immutable audit log with timestamp and actor, so that all payment activity is traceable and verifiable.

stories.title: As a system, I want to retain payment audit logs for a minimum of 7 years, so that financial compliance standards are met.
stories.story_statement: As a system, I want to retain payment audit logs for a minimum of 7 years, so that financial compliance standards are met.
stories.business_value: Meets regulatory requirements for long-term audit trail retention.

acceptance_criteria.when: The system is queried for audit logs after 7 years.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system retains the log for at least 7 years and makes it accessible for compliance audits.

stories.title: As a system, I want to maintain order state during temporary Stripe API unavailability, so that no orders are lost during outages.
stories.story_statement: As a system, I want to maintain order state during temporary Stripe API unavailability, so that no orders are lost during outages.

acceptance_criteria.when: The system attempts to process a payment request.

stories.title: As a system, I want to define what constitutes 'normal load' for webhook processing, so that the 2-second response time is met under realistic conditions.
stories.story_statement: As a system, I want to define what constitutes 'normal load' for webhook processing, so that the 2-second response time is met under realistic conditions.
stories.business_value: Provides a clear benchmark for performance testing and ensures consistent response times.

acceptance_criteria.given: The system is under normal load conditions (e.g., 100 concurrent webhooks).
acceptance_criteria.when: A webhook callback is delivered to the endpoint.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system processes the callback and completes the response within 2 seconds.

stories.title: As a system, I want to record the provider's failure reason code for every failed payment attempt, so that failure details are available for debugging and analysis.
stories.story_statement: As a system, I want to record the provider's failure reason code for every failed payment attempt, so that failure details are available for debugging and analysis.

acceptance_criteria.then: The system records the failure reason code in the payment record with the exact format specified by Stripe.

stories.title: As a system, I want to define the content and delivery mechanism for refund email notifications to customers, so that customers receive clear and timely updates.
stories.story_statement: As a system, I want to define the content and delivery mechanism for refund email notifications to customers, so that customers receive clear and timely updates.
stories.business_value: Improves customer communication and satisfaction with refund updates.

acceptance_criteria.given: A refund is successfully issued by a support agent.
acceptance_criteria.when: The system processes the refund completion event.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system sends an email to the customer with content including the refund amount, date, and reference number, delivered via SMTP or a supported email service.

stories.title: As a system, I want to define what 'immutable' means and how the audit log is implemented, so that data integrity is preserved over time.
stories.story_statement: As a system, I want to define what 'immutable' means and how the audit log is implemented, so that data integrity is preserved over time.
stories.business_value: Ensures that audit logs cannot be altered or deleted after creation, supporting compliance and accountability.

acceptance_criteria.given: A payment state transition occurs (e.g., pending to authorized).
acceptance_criteria.when: The system logs the transition in the audit log.
acceptance_criteria.then: The log entry is stored in a write-once-read-many format (e.g., database with immutable table) and cannot be modified or deleted after creation.

stories.title: As a system, I want to define the expected behavior when a webhook is received after the order has been fulfilled, so that order state is not incorrectly updated.
stories.story_statement: As a system, I want to define the expected behavior when a webhook is received after the order has been fulfilled, so that order state is not incorrectly updated.
stories.business_value: Prevents incorrect updates to order status after fulfillment, maintaining data consistency.

acceptance_criteria.given: A webhook callback is received after the order has been fulfilled.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system ignores the callback and does not update the order status or trigger any fulfillment actions.

stories.title: As a system, I want to define the behavior when a customer attempts to refund a payment that is still in a 'pending' state, so that refund functionality is only available for completed payments.
stories.story_statement: As a system, I want to define the behavior when a customer attempts to refund a payment that is still in a 'pending' state, so that refund functionality is only available for completed payments.
stories.business_value: Ensures refunds are only available when the payment has been completed and captured.

acceptance_criteria.given: A customer attempts to refund a payment that is still in a 'pending' state.
acceptance_criteria.when: The system processes the refund request.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system rejects the request and informs the customer that refunds are only available for completed payments.

technical_tasks.description: Implement Stripe integration to process card payments using Stripe's API endpoints.
Implement webhook signature verification using a shared secret configured with Stripe at deployment time.
Create a payment record in a 'pending' state before redirecting the customer to the payment provider.
Record every payment state transition in an immutable audit log with timestamp and actor.
Store the provider's failure reason code for every failed payment attempt.
Ensure payment audit logs are retained for a minimum of 7 years to meet financial compliance standards.
Implement idempotency logic to prevent double-crediting of orders from out-of-order or duplicate webhook deliveries.
Expose a webhook endpoint to receive asynchronous payment status callbacks from Stripe.
Ensure the system does not store raw card numbers to comply with PCI-DSS scope reduction via Stripe-hosted card entry.
Define and implement the behavior when a webhook is received after the order has been fulfilled.
Define and implement the behavior when a customer attempts to refund a payment that is still in a 'pending' state.
Implement email notification content and delivery mechanism for refund notifications to customers.
Define what 'immutable' means and how the audit log is implemented to ensure data integrity over time.
Define what constitutes 'normal load' for webhook processing to ensure the 2-second response time is met under realistic conditions.
Ensure that refunds are only available when a payment has been in a 'captured' state.

risks.description: A prolonged Stripe outage could block all new order payments platform-wide.
risks.mitigation: Implement a fallback mechanism or queue to handle order creation during Stripe unavailability, with a clear timeout and retry policy.
risks.contingency: If Stripe remains unavailable for more than 15 minutes, automatically mark all new orders as 'payment unavailable' and notify support.

risks.description: The definition of 'normal load' for webhook processing is not clearly defined.
risks.mitigation: Define 'normal load' as 100 concurrent webhook requests per second with 95% of requests completing within 2 seconds.
risks.contingency: If actual load exceeds defined normal load, trigger a scaling event or alert the operations team.

risks.description: The format of the failure reason code for failed payments is not specified.
risks.mitigation: Use Stripe's official error codes (e.g., 'card_error', 'invalid_card') as the format for recording failure reason codes.
risks.contingency: If Stripe changes its error codes, maintain a mapping table and update it with each version change.

risks.description: The expected email notification content and delivery mechanism for refunds is not specified.
risks.mitigation: Use a standard refund email template with subject line 'Refund Issued' and include order ID, amount, and refund date.
risks.contingency: If email delivery fails, log the failure and notify support with a retry mechanism.

risks.description: The definition of 'immutable audit log' and its implementation method is not defined.
risks.mitigation: Implement the audit log in a write-once-read-many database with immutable storage using a time-based immutable log structure.
risks.contingency: If the database fails, store logs in a separate immutable storage (e.g., encrypted file system or blockchain) with versioned backups.

risks.description: The maximum duration for audit log retention is not specified.
risks.mitigation: Retain logs for a minimum of 7 years as required, with no upper limit specified.
risks.contingency: If regulatory changes require longer retention, update the retention policy and notify stakeholders.

risks.description: The expected behavior if a webhook is received after fulfillment is not defined.
risks.mitigation: Log the event and ignore the webhook if the order has already been fulfilled.
risks.contingency: If the system processes such a webhook, implement a validation rule to check order fulfillment status before processing.

risks.description: The behavior when a payment is in a 'pending' state and a refund is attempted is not defined.
risks.mitigation: Reject refund requests for payments in a 'pending' state with a clear error message.
risks.contingency: If a refund is attempted, redirect to a support agent for manual handling with a flag to prevent future attempts.

assumptions.description: The system will be accessible via a public internet-facing endpoint to receive webhooks and serve customer-facing pages.
